restrictions: Messages are exactly 135 bytes; each is one padded block M || 0x86 with zero capacity (520 fixed state bits). Complete fixed-zero-IV SHA3-256 sponge with suffix 0x06 and pad10*1, prefix rounds 0..4, 256-bit digest.

This package is rubenmarcus's v15 (91f1424d, itself winglock's v14 f1cedf6b with Th0rgal) with three changes and nothing else: (1) P's T3 runs as counted programs: hv_step tabulates each half vector together with all 127 keys of the 7 levels (one Gray step XORs 7 plane words and 15 key words; 96 counted primitives on its longest path, replacing the bounds 2^7 per half vector plus 2^11 per half vector per level), and match_step forms alpha2, its active-row count and the AS <= nb - 1 decision (83 counted primitives, replacing the bound 2^9); the keys, matches and decisions are exactly v15's (r5-mitm-1 trials 1 and 2), so P's output and its 7,251,935 matches are v15's.

v16 change (2): the caps X_MAX = 2^20 work units per connector attempt (v15: 2^23) and S2CAP = 2^21 stage-2 pairs per space (v15: 2^24), set by v13's run-free cap rule (each cap the largest power of two whose charged term stays within a reference term, here 2^40 primitives = v15's P charge 2^40.43 rounded down; v13 used v14's T3 batch term, which no longer exists). No R5 or R6 run comes near either cap (largest attempt 190,240 work units, largest stage-2 count 315), so every R5 and R6 run is a complete run of v16 and its success indicator is v16's.

v16 change (3): development is repriced by the rule v14 and v15 already use (counted prices of the submitted programs): v15's D15 at v16's counted T3 prices (2^34.6617 -> 2^32.2995, conservative: rounded-up inputs, items without a T3 breakdown kept at v15's charge), plus our own D16 (2^27 units, a stated bound). B', S, the connector, the driver, K = 96, A_ADV, A_MAX, B_BUDGET, CCAP, M_CAP, E and the success studies are v15's, unchanged.

No advice: the algorithm runs every phase itself, and its time is the sum of caps, fixed counts and organizer-recomputed counts times counted prices or stated bounds (proof 2, 6): P 2^29.0537 units (T1, T2 as in v14; T3: 48,592,224 half vectors at 96 counted primitives each including all keys, 127 blocks of sort and merge at 2^6 per half vector, matches capped at M_CAP = 2^24 at 83 counted primitives plus a 2^11 evaluation bound); B' 2^32 units plus one update; at most 2^13 connector attempts of at most X_MAX = 2^20 work units (2^29.4539); E: K = 96 spaces, setup at most 2^16 units, 2^24 Gray steps of 364 counted primitives per 256 pairs (2^28.6887), at most S2CAP = 2^21 stage-2 pairs per space (2^29.3970). Algorithm 2^32.6503.

Development is charged as preprocessing by v14's rule (proof 0.1, H2): every target-specific run whose result fixed, or under its plan could have changed, a number the algorithm reads, at the counted prices of the submitted programs. v14's G2 (2^31.8877) and C (2^33.2426) as in v15; v15's D15 repriced at v16's counted T3 programs (2^32.2995; at v15's own prices 2^34.6617); our D16 (2^27, bound). Total 2^34.6142, claimed 34.62; preprocessing 34.51. Sensitivities, not claimed: v15's caps 35.05; D15 at v15's prices 35.49; D15 doubled 34.88; D16 sixteen times larger 34.72.

Premise P (inside H1; success only): P outputs the trail of proof 3 within M_CAP. P's native run certified it at its level of 64 blocks (W* = 127 <= 2 x 64 - 1, Lemma P: every leaf with AS(alpha2) <= 63 is found, every other leaf has w1 >= 128), with 7,251,935 matches; the organizer recomputes the structural counts, the output core's level (r5-count trial 10), seed-picked cores (r5-mitm-0, 1) and P's driver on a sub-problem with its cap. If P certified nothing it would output nothing; every cost bound holds either way.

Probability space: the algorithm's own coins (B' candidate coins, connector coins), fixed target, no advice. Success is measured end to end (proof 5): R6, our pre-registration (plan and code hashed before any run, 48 complete runs of v15, all reported; each is also a complete run of v16, Lemma 6): 44 of 48 succeed, one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound 0.8193. R5, v14's pre-registration, consists of complete runs of v15 (Lemma 6): 46 of 48, bound 0.874. Claimed 0.40; each study alone supports it.

Executed evidence (not the claimed cost): R6 and R5 (proof 4.2, 4.7, Appendices D, E), with 7 R6 and 8 R5 collisions as certificates; r5-R-0..7 re-derive 16 seed-picked R5 successes per review; r5-bpfull runs a whole B' from its label; r5-count checks the counted stage 1 step by step against plain evaluation and its longest path, the T2 leaf, P's driver and cap, P's certifying level on the output core; (new in v16) r5-mitm-1 (trials 1, 2) checks the counted half-vector step over both full half tables of the output core (118,096 steps, longest path 96, vectors, keys of all 7 levels and w2 equal to the plain tables at sampled steps) and the counted match step on every level-64 match of the output core in 4 seed-picked blocks (longest path 83, AS and decision equal to the plain evaluation); r5-trail-0..3 recount T1, T2 and the half vectors.

rubenmarcus's v15 (91f1424d) is the base: its T3 meet-in-the-middle, counted stage 1, D15 and R6 are theirs. Th0rgal (7deb1595, with Subflatus3 and rubenmarcus) introduced the zero-advice framing; winglock's v8, v13, v14 built the algorithm; Subflatus3 (9bccf245) the zero-block half-sum match. Memory: largest phase about 2^28 bytes (key words add 15 x 32 bytes per half-vector entry, at most 2 x 9^5 entries per core: under 60 MB); declared 30.

The nominal reference identifier does not assert an improvement over published work; no improvement on the method of Guo et al. is claimed beyond the byte-aligned adaptation, B', the counted programs and the accounting.

heuristics.statement: Averaged over all of the algorithm's own coins (B' candidate coins, connector coins), the probability p that v16's algorithm outputs a collision satisfies p >= 0.40. Premise R (run selection and coins): the SHA-256/SHAKE-256 coins of labels fixed before the runs act as fresh coins, and the 48 runs of each pre-registered study (R6, ours; R5, v14's) are an unselected sample of the algorithm's runs, so that their success indicators are independent Bernoulli(p) draws. Premise P: P outputs the trail of proof Section 3 within M_CAP.
heuristics.scope: Only the success probability. Each R6 and R5 run is a complete run of v16 with label-derived coins (proof Lemma 6): v16 differs from v15 only in the programs that compute P's T3 (same keys, matches and decisions, r5-mitm-1 trials 1-2) and in the caps X_MAX = 2^20 and S2CAP = 2^21, which no R5 or R6 run reached (largest attempt 190,240 work units, largest stage-2 count 315). Each R6 run is a complete run of v15 with label-derived coins (proof Lemma 6a: v14's B', connector and driver code, P's certified trail, E as fes with stage 2 and S2CAP; no cap that should not act acted), and each R5 run is one too (Lemma 6b: v15 computes v14's outputs). Premise P concerns success only: every cost term of P is a fixed count, an organizer-recomputed count or a cap. Output correctness and every cost cap hold without H1.
heuristics.extrapolation: R6: 44 of 48 runs succeed; under premise R the one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound is 0.8193, so by R6's pre-registered rule the claim 0.40 is supported. R5: 46 of 48, bound 0.8746. The studies are not pooled. Premise R: R6's plan, driver, analysis, launcher, enumerator and P program were hashed at 2026-10-08T00:19:33Z before any run and made read-only; every run is reported (proof 4.7, Appendix E: per-run ledger with result-file hashes); the plan's only outcome-dependent rule is whether to claim; every other run made for v15 is listed (proof 4.1). Premise P: P's native run certifies the trail by Lemma P; it agrees with v14's exhaustive T3 passes; the organizer re-runs the output core's certifying level, seed-picked cores and P's driver on a sub-problem. Organizer checks of R5 as in v14 (r5-R-0..7, r5-bpfull); 7 R6 and 8 R5 collisions are certificates.
heuristics.limitations: Label-seeded SHAKE-256 coins stand in for fresh words (premise R). R6's failures, run order and timing are logged by us; the organizer re-derives no R6 run (the experiment file's 64-KiB budget holds only R5's table), but 7 R6 collisions are certificates. R5's limitations are v14's. P's full-scale certification rests on our native run (296 CPU-s, reproducible from Appendix A); the organizer checks 3 of 467 cores per review at the certifying level.

heuristics.statement: The charged development - v14's G2 (2^31.8877 units) and C (2^33.2426 units) as in v15, v15's D15 repriced at the counted prices of v16's T3 programs (2^32.2995 units), and our D16 (2^27 units, bound) - contains every target-specific run whose result fixed, or under its plan could have changed, a number that v16's algorithm reads, and these prices are the ones the cost model requires. The caps X_MAX and S2CAP were set by v13's run-free rule, not by a run. Every other run either produced program text or fixed no number of v16.
heuristics.scope: Only the development (preprocessing) part of the time and preprocessing claims. The algorithm's own terms (2^32.6503) are caps, fixed counts and recomputed counts at counted prices or stated bounds, and do not depend on H2.
heuristics.extrapolation: Proof 0.1 lists every run (v15's list, unchanged, plus D16). D15 at v16's prices is a function of v15's own published D15 itemization only (v15 proof 0.1, reproduced in proof V.3): in each item the match term, which v15 charged at 2^9 primitives per match, is charged at 83, the key term at the counted half-vector step, and every other part is kept at v15's price; where v15 states only a rounded charge we take it rounded up, which can only raise the result. No D15 workload is reconstructed or re-run by us, so H2 for D15 rests on exactly the evidence that supported v15's D15. Proof 0.2 gives the origin of every new number of v15: analysis, counting, or a charged run (D15). G2 and C are priced at v15's E by v14's own rule (the search, if added to the submitted program, runs on its counted routines); C's spaces were computed by fes.c, which is v15's stage 1. D15 charges our abandoned contiguous-block T3 run as if its last level had completed (its match count recounted without enumeration) and every other development run of v15 at P's prices.
heuristics.limitations: Repricing D15 at v16's programs is the same rule v15 applied to G2 and C; at v15's prices D15 gives 35.49, still below 35.76. The caps rule's reference term (2^40 primitives) is v15's P charge rounded down; with v15's caps the total is 35.05. At v14's prices for G2 and C the total is 37.13, above v14's 37.05: the improvement depends on accepting v14's pricing rule for development as applied to v15's programs. A1 (v7's design study that produced B''s code) stays uncharged as in v14; charging it gives 40.98. D15's largest item is an upper bound (the stopped run is charged complete).
